derivation: LIFE-010 names this the directional special case: LATE_AFTER_RELEASE is established effect evidence following an authorized no-effect release for the same provider-native operation identity, permit and stable dispatch-attempt digest. All three hold here, so the classification is LATE_AFTER_RELEASE rather than CONFLICTING. The record carries no mismatch of its own: the request matched the permit, the attempt was eligible, and LATE_AFTER_RELEASE is not among the classifications that force completion_mismatch true. RES-WIRE-003's reconciliation table gives a RELEASED reservation receiving a later EFFECT the EFFECT_DISPUTED decision: it becomes DISPUTED, restores the unresolved pending charge, retains the actual effect and blocks the affected partition. RES-WIRE-004 makes LATE_EFFECT_AFTER_RELEASE take precedence over the native record's mismatch reason. LIFE-006's mapping contributes LATE_EFFECT_AFTER_RELEASE for the classification and adds BUDGET_EFFECT_DISPUTED with the receipt reason, which coincide, so the sorted set has two members. LIFE-013 makes the two outcomes name one another in symmetric conflict lists. LIFE-012 bars the late evidence from erasing the earlier closure or reopening completed routing, so the NO_EFFECT completed row and the selected failure route are unchanged.
